note: COPY THIS FILE TO START A NEW SCENARIO. One line = one reading + how long it holds. `hold_ms` is SIMULATED time, so this whole file is a 7-minute machine history that a test replays in under a millisecond. Frame 1: twenty seconds of a cool, healthy machine.

Frame 2: two minutes at `fair`. Held long enough, this is what engages the duty cycle. `cpu_speed_limit_pct` is optional and defaults to 100 (`no cap recorded`), so you only write it when the scenario is ABOUT throttling.
Frame 3: two minutes at `serious` — the pause tier. Valid states are exactly: nominal, fair, serious, critical (plus any other string, which is deliberately treated as WORSE than critical).
Frame 4: the `battery` key is optional and independent of `thermal`. Omit it entirely to simulate a desktop with no battery. Here the charge drops, on battery, while the machine is still warm.
Frame 5: OMITTING `thermal` is not a mistake — it is the reading the OS failed to produce, which the governor treats as `time passed, no new information`. Use it to simulate a probe gap.

Frame 6: cool again, back on the charger. THE LAST FRAME HOLDS FOREVER — a run that outlasts the scenario stays at the last condition you stated, so always end with the condition you want the tail of the run to see.
